question: What is the primary purpose of nursing data integration in healthcare informatics?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for nursing documentation
options.B: To combine data from multiple clinical sources into a unified view of patient health
options.C: To restrict patient information access exclusively to hospital administrators
options.D: To replace direct bedside nursing care with automated software programs

explanation: Data integration specifically involves combining data from multiple clinical sources to provide a unified, comprehensive view of a patient's health status. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h1)

question: How does data integration directly benefit daily nursing workflows?

options.A: It increases the time spent searching for missing paper records
options.B: It decreases the need for shift handovers between nurses
options.C: It reduces time spent looking for missing records so nurses can focus on patient care
options.D: It eliminates the requirement to record vital signs and fluid balances

explanation: When data flows seamlessly between departments, nurses spend less time searching for missing records and more time delivering direct patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h1)

question: In the context of the DIKW hierarchy, what best describes a raw patient temperature reading of 38.5°柏?
explanation: Data represents raw, uninterpreted facts or observations, such as a single temperature reading before it is contextualized. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why is a data dictionary important in healthcare information systems?

options.A: It provides standardized definitions so terms mean the same thing across all clinical units
options.B: It translates medical terminology into foreign languages for international patients
options.C: It stores historical patient billing records for insurance companies
options.D: It automatically prescribes medications based on patient vital signs

explanation: A data dictionary ensures that every term used across a health system has a standardized definition, preventing miscommunication between different clinical units. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of standardized nursing terminologies in electronic health records?

options.A: To replace physician diagnoses with nursing diagnoses entirely
options.B: To capture nursing diagnoses, interventions, and outcomes systematically and make nursing work visible
options.C: To increase the amount of time spent writing unstructured narrative notes
options.D: To eliminate the need for patient assessment and vital sign documentation

explanation: Standardized terminologies provide structured, coded vocabularies specifically designed to capture nursing diagnoses, interventions, and outcomes systematically, making nursing contributions visible. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is a widely recognized classification system specifically used for nursing diagnoses?
explanation: NANDA-International (NANDA-I) is the leading recognized terminology framework specifically utilized for identifying and classifying nursing diagnoses. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary role of interoperability standards in healthcare data systems?

options.A: To ensure that software from different vendors can securely communicate and share data
options.B: To restrict patient data exchange exclusively to paper-based transmission
options.C: To increase the cost of purchasing electronic health record software
options.D: To prevent nurses from accessing laboratory and pharmacy records

explanation: Interoperability standards allow disparate health information systems from different vendors to communicate, share, and interpret data seamlessly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which level of interoperability ensures that the clinical meaning of exchanged data is fully understood by both receiving and sending systems?
explanation: Semantic interoperability ensures that the meaning of the exchanged data is shared and correctly interpreted by both participating systems. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is a major benefit of embedded Clinical Decision Support (CDS) tools within an EHR system?

options.A: They completely automate all physical nursing assessments without human input
options.B: They provide real-time alerts and prompts, such as sepsis screening or drug-allergy warnings
options.C: They restrict nurses from accessing patient medication administration histories
options.D: They replace the need for standardized nursing terminologies and classifications

explanation: Clinical Decision Support tools provide real-time alerts and safety prompts, such as drug-allergy warnings or sepsis screening reminders, directly within the EHR. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h5)

question: How does proper EHR data architecture directly impact the nursing workflow?

options.A: By organizing information logically so nurses can quickly retrieve vital sign trends and patient histories
options.B: By hiding patient laboratory results to protect hospital privacy policies
options.C: By requiring nurses to document the same patient assessment in three different formats
options.D: By slowing down computer processing speeds during emergency admissions

explanation: A well-organized data architecture determines how quickly and efficiently a nurse can retrieve vital sign trends, medication histories, and lab results. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h5)

question: What does data integrity primarily ensure within an electronic health record system?

options.A: That data remains unaltered, uncorrupted, and reliable throughout its lifecycle
options.B: That all patient records are permanently deleted after discharge
options.C: That only hospital administrators have permission to read nursing notes
options.D: That patient data can be freely shared on public social media platforms

explanation: Data integrity ensures that information remains uncorrupted, reliable, and unaltered throughout storage, transmission, and retrieval. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following represents an automated data validation technique used to prevent documentation errors?

options.A: Allowing nurses to copy and paste previous patient notes without review
options.B: Range checks that prevent entering impossible physiological values, such as a heart rate of 900 bpm
options.C: Delaying the documentation of vital signs until the end of a 12-hour shift
options.D: Removing all drop-down menus in favor of unstructured narrative text

explanation: Automated range checks act as validation safeguards that prevent clinicians from entering physically impossible physiological values into the system. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of role-based access control (RBAC) in electronic health record systems?

options.A: To ensure nurses only access patient records relevant to their specific care duties
options.B: To grant every hospital employee unrestricted access to all patient charts
options.C: To allow patients to edit their own medical diagnoses and laboratory results
options.D: To prevent physicians from documenting patient care plans in the EHR

explanation: Role-based access control restricts system access so that healthcare workers, including nurses, can only view records necessary for their specific clinical responsibilities. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why are system audit trails important in maintaining healthcare data security?

options.A: They automatically prescribe medications based on audit findings
options.B: They track and record every instance a user views, edits, or deletes a patient record to ensure accountability
options.C: They permanently erase patient history after every shift change
options.D: They replace the need for passwords and secure login credentials

explanation: Audit trails record every user interaction with patient records, providing accountability and helping detect unauthorized access or snooping. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h7)

question: How does integrated nursing data directly contribute to enhanced patient safety?

options.A: By allowing earlier detection of clinical deterioration and reducing medication administration errors
options.B: By increasing the frequency of redundant charting across multiple paper logs
options.C: By removing clinical decision support tools from the electronic health record
options.D: By limiting communication between nurses and physicians during emergencies

explanation: Holistic, integrated data provides real-time visibility that allows for earlier detection of clinical deterioration and helps reduce medication errors. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h8)

question: What is a major workflow benefit experienced by nurses when patient data is effectively integrated?

options.A: An increase in administrative paperwork and duplicate documentation
options.B: Elimination of redundant charting and reduced time spent hunting for scattered information
options.C: The complete removal of shift handovers and verbal communication
options.D: Mandatory reliance on manual paper-based vital sign tracking

explanation: Effective data integration eliminates redundant charting and reduces time spent searching for scattered information, allowing more time for direct patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h8)
